adoptionSource: The project owner adopted revision 1 (7bce50fc) and subsequently specified OpenCode 2.x APIs exclusively, released A2UI 1.0, and the latest compatible stable AG-UI. The signed superseding binding identifies when this proposal is authorized for implementation.
amendmentPolicy: Any later change to scope, evidence, fixture identity, limits or scenario uses an explicit owner-approved superseding decision. Preserve the consumed budget and original receipts.

releaseClaim.userOperation: Continue chatting after external Codex login or managed expiry; use a V2 OpenCode provider with the user's verified Pro allowance; select either native REST harness, use embedded chat and validated surfaces, and administer supported modes and local clients.
supportedEnvironments: Native macOS service-host and Linux release container with an explicit host-owned or dedicated file-backed Codex store

Local-owner and authenticated shared deployments using Codex CLI/SDK 0.169.0 and OpenCode 2.x. Host, SDK and plugin 2.3.0 are the first certification target. Record tested triples and treat other combinations as unverified.

Embedded React 19/Vite 8 with A2UI wire 1.0 exclusively, canonical schema at 28e3d6bd4fb21a38be5abb0959bf73fd9708ffe0, @a2ui/react and @a2ui/web_core 0.15.0, @ag-ui/client and @ag-ui/core 1.0.5, and the @ag-ui/a2ui-middleware 0.0.16 bridge contract. Capture actual host/editor/CLI versions.
releaseClaim.currentCapabilities: Existing Rust service provides direct REST, streaming text, basic MCP/ACP and optional A2A discovery and memory. Startup snapshots credentials, OpenCode uses V1 hooks and the embedded UI is absent at the analysis baseline.
explicitUnknowns: Live Pro allowance attribution and availability of a dedicated account are unverified.
Native keyring/host broker and release worker support must be demonstrated for each claimed deployment.
Actual installed client versions, shared identity provider and entitled models are measured during verification.

oracle.observation: Skills cap, schema-vs-executor labels, emitted hooks, DB and embedding billing state, card availability and runtime topology match the effective settings.
oracle.expectedTruthSource: Known document owner and markers, webhook capture, selected skill marker and independent reader of the A2A card.
oracle.comparator: Compare independently observed delivery, retrieval and discovery against the source configuration. Check memory authorization for list, search, injection and deletion as both users.

negativeControl.input: Use a foreign document ID or spoofed scope, disable or misconfigure the DB/hooks, and request a delivery to an unapproved destination.
negativeControl.expectedRejection: No foreign document access, injection, deletion or unauthorized egress. Degraded, disabled or pending-restart state stays visible.

scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Unique private run root, isolated HOME, CODEX_HOME, XDG config/data roots, two workspaces, loopback ports and client profiles. Non-secret seed manifest .kbd-orchestrator/phases/codex-live-auth-opencode-console/fixture-manifest.json SHA-256 2cf1435fffc9117147c71693cf87967148c5464c471121ed4faf1e1e240af97b. Record hashes of realized non-secret fixtures, installed executable, image and client versions. Keep bearer and grant values out of receipts.
scenarioMatrix.evidence: Run-local FEATURE-1 receipt with build/config digests, versions, actor, argv, exit status, monotonic timing, independent observation and negative-control evidence. Record each required client, transport and deployment subcase individually.
limitations: A synthetic webhook proves local dispatch, not availability of arbitrary external destinations.

functionalScope: External login updates running requests without a restart.
Expired credentials recover once while preserving identity and billing.
Late refresh cannot resurrect a signed-out or superseded account.
An installed V2 provider completes an attributable subscription turn.
Both selectable REST drivers preserve session ownership and native cancellation.
Authorized native tool effects occur once and denied effects never occur.
Installed binary and image serve usable accessible chat and settings.
Validated structured surfaces render, update and dispatch one authorized action.
All 16 settings areas report effective behavior and enforce privileges.
OpenCode config changes preserve user files in project and global scope.
Supported editors launch the installed ACP agent and display a prompt update.
Five named clients discover and call the configured MCP server.
Skills, tool schemas, hooks, memory and discovery agree with real runtime behavior.

resilienceScope.policy: Mandatory resilience includes logout/switch during refresh, unknown exchange outcome, partial store writes, mount replacement, session cancellation/replay, worker restart, tool duplication, foreign actions, stale configurations and degraded/unavailable features. These remain acceptance obligations if a prerequisite is missing or a budget is exhausted.
deferredOptional: Additional unlisted ACP/MCP client adapters and unverified operating systems
A remote OpenCode SDK attach driver
Further A2UI wire versions or unregistered catalogs

exclusions: Using a shared operator subscription for chat users or automatically falling back to separate paid API billing
Silent arbitrary function passthrough over the pinned Codex SDK
Public registry publication, changing personal workstation configurations during Spec, and automatic deployment

OpenCode V1 plugin/SDK dependencies, legacy hooks, V1 config mutation and downgrade paths. This limit applies to OpenCode, independently of the proxy's OpenAI-compatible HTTP routes and versioned conversation API.
A2UI drafts, v0.9 and unregistered catalogs on the structured endpoint. The legacy AG-UI plain-text route stays available.

requiredSafetyChecks.description: Refresh, reload, recovery and native session resume preserve the authenticated owner, routing generation and authorized upstream with redacted credentials.
An unauthorized allowance cannot be charged and a tool effect cannot be duplicated, replayed or run outside an approved workspace.
Check direct API authorization and origin protection, owner-scoped files and memory, fail-closed concurrent writes, cleanup and redaction.
Plain text never creates executable UI. Invalid catalogs, frames, cross-user actions and duplicate activation cannot trigger privileged behavior.

budgets.tokenFallback: Time, tool-call, repair and no-progress ceilings bound the consolidated verification run; retain historical consumption.
budgets.exhaustion: Checkpoint and mark BLOCKED; preserve unresolved effects and receipts and request a budget amendment before further attempts.

evidenceInvalidation: Record contract, spec, relevant source, package, config, method and non-secret fixture hashes. Invalidate only affected scenario evidence on change. Retain earlier receipts with their original identities.

workerRoutes.model: Active Codex harness for production owners; isolated service reviewer for contract and acceptance review.
workerRoutes.billing: No provider charge is authorized by specifying or adopting this contract. Require separate consent for real subscription turns or paid embedding evidence.
workerRoutes.subagents: Identity, OpenCode extensions, chat experience, runtime, build/release and independent service reviewer work through scoped ownership.

expectedEffects: Build the actual native and image distributions with clean/default and optional memory configuration; capture zero-warning Cargo baseline, clippy, unit and plugin typecheck results separately.
Start only isolated native workers and disposable service/client profiles, exercise each positive and negative subcase with real collaborators, then restore resources.

Run checks through the installed package. Reading files or mocked success does not prove real login, subscription billing, native cancellation, editor registration, browser rendering, or deployed outcomes.
boundaryPacket.requiredApprovals: Separate owner authorization before live subscriber/paid operations or a machine-level change. Only disposable client profiles and an explicitly consented account may be used. Spec and contract adoption do not authorize running the boundary.
receipts: Per-run private manifest including exact executable/versions and subcase digests
Local redacted per-scenario evidence with independent expected/observed values, effects and controls
Restoration and cleanup record, failed/missing prerequisites, no account secrets
cleanup: Use trap/finally to stop suite children and restore files even if an earlier command fails.
Dispose of scratch credentials and owned client entries, preserve only redacted output. Reconcile any indeterminate effect before retrying.
stopConditions: Any boundary without prerequisites, consent, identity or isolation is BLOCKED; a case not attempted is NOT_EXERCISED.
Unintended external charge/write, credential disclosure, or foreign account action stops subsequent affected work and requires reconciliation.
Exit zero alone is insufficient. Record each required subcase, a real failed oracle as FAIL, and any unresolved effects or exhausted budget.
